parts.text: A page of printed text is placed 18 cm from a converging lens of focal length 35 cm. Fig. 6.1 is a scale diagram of the arrangement with each of the two principal focuses (focal points) of the lens labelled F. Fig. 6.1

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) A length of 1.0 cm on the scale diagram represents an actual length of 5.0 cm.

parts.label: i
parts.text: (i) By drawing on Fig. 6.1, locate the image of the page produced by the lens and label it I . [3]

ms.label: 6(a)(i)
ms.text:
any two from:
•
ray from top / bottom of object, parallel to principal axis, refracted through right-hand principal focus
•
straight ray from same point on object through optical centre
•
ray that (seems to) come from left-hand principal focus through same point of object and refracted parallel to principal
axis
rays traced back to intersection AND intersection / image labelled I

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Using Fig. 6.1, determine the actual distance of image I from the lens. actual distance from lens = ......................................................... [2]

ms.label: 6(a)(ii)
ms.text:
(distance = ) 35.5 cm to 38.5 cm
7.1 to 7.7 (cm) OR (distance =) 35.0 (cm) to 40.0 (cm)

ms.label: 6(b)
ms.text:
virtual AND any one from:
•
cannot be projected on a screen
•
(real) light (ray) does not pass through image
•
light only seems to come from image

ms.label: 6(c)
ms.text:
any one from:
•
long-sightedness focuses image behind retina / back of eye OR longsightedness produces blurry / fuzzy images (of
close objects)
•
converging lens reduces focal length (of eye)
•
(converging lens) puts image further away (from the eye)
(converging lens gives) sharp/focussed image on retina / back of eye OR (with lens) rays converge on retina / back of eye
